cases.prompt: Several equipment products need a shared command, state and device framework with product-specific workflows.
required_behaviors: recognizes reusable capability, variation and extension-contract pressures
requires real boundaries before abstraction
forbidden_behaviors: creates base classes only because names repeat
mixes product UI into the reusable core
baseline_expected_failure: agent proposes generic inheritance without contracts
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, evidence, and omissions; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Design shared device/protocol capability for general, keypad and customer-specific touch utilities.
required_behaviors: separates stable core from product composition and policy
defines extension points, lifecycle and compatibility contracts
controls capability granted to plug-ins
addresses versioning and test matrix
forbidden_behaviors: uses copied project trees as the product-line model
passes a powerful global façade to every extension
baseline_expected_failure: agent creates feature flags without ownership or release semantics
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, evidence, and omissions; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: One small application has one stable implementation and no foreseeable variation. Add abstractions for future reuse.
required_behaviors: rejects speculative framework extraction
keeps the implementation simple unless a real pressure exists
forbidden_behaviors: introduces plug-ins or factories without variation
baseline_expected_failure: agent applies framework patterns merely for cleanliness
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, evidence, and omissions; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Create a shared equipment kernel for several products whose chamber composition, UI and workflows vary by configuration.
required_behaviors: separates stable command/state/capability contracts from product composition and workflow policy
defines config schema/version and extension lifecycle
defines source/package/binary authority and consumer compatibility
forbidden_behaviors: uses copied DLLs or project trees as the product-line contract
turns configuration into unrestricted behavior without governance
baseline_expected_failure: agent centralizes all product behavior into one framework
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, authority, lifecycle, failure behavior, and evidence; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Design one reusable device framework for products that use different transports and discover implementations through a registry consumed by several hosts.
required_behaviors: models transport-independent capabilities and preserves transport-specific limits, lifecycle and failure semantics
defines one authoritative registry with a shared adapter and enumerated consumers
requires positive propagation and negative drift-injection tests for registry changes
forbidden_behaviors: forces every transport into a lowest-common-denominator interface
copies registry entries or switch statements into each consumer
claims registry centralization is sufficient without mutation evidence
required_artifacts: registry authority and anti-drift test plan
baseline_expected_failure: agent centralizes a registry structurally but does not prove propagation or detect consumer drift
cases.review_notes: The closest authoritative-contract pattern requires both positive propagation and negative injected-drift coverage.

cases.prompt: We have a reusable PeriodicWorkerMixin used by several products: a scheduler thread calls the subclass's on_tick() repeatedly, and rechecks self._paused / self._stopped / self._cancel_token only in between those calls -- pause(), stop() and cancel() never interrupt a call to on_tick() itself. Design a subclass override of on_tick() for a device-polling product that must drain an entire incoming command queue, processing every queued command before returning control to the scheduler.
required_behaviors: identifies that an on_tick() override draining the whole queue in one call runs its own indefinite internal loop and defeats the mixin's pause/stop/cancellation flags, since those are only rechecked between ticks
bounds each override invocation to one unit of work (e.g. one command, or one small fixed-size chunk) and lets the scheduler drive repeated calls to process the rest
requires verifying that pause()/stop()/cancel() actually take effect within one tick interval, not only after an unbounded override finishes on its own
flags this as a required check for every override of the mixin's per-tick callback, not just this one product
forbidden_behaviors: implements or accepts an on_tick() override with an internal while/for loop that only returns once the queue is empty
assumes the mixin's cooperative flags will interrupt the override mid-loop without the override itself checking them
treats the long-draining override as merely a performance concern rather than a silent breakage of pause/stop/cancellation
baseline_expected_failure: agent writes on_tick() with an internal loop that drains the full queue before returning, unaware this blocks the mixin's pause/stop checks until the loop finishes on its own
cases.review_notes: Closes the new Framework Failure Modes bullet on periodic/worker mixin overrides that run their own indefinite internal loop instead of returning promptly each tick.

cases.prompt: A MediaPlayer class composes two reusable bases: PlaybackController, a domain interface with play(), stop(), pause() and resume() for playback state, and ThreadWorkerMixin, a generic utility that also declares start(), stop(), pause() and resume() to control its own background processing thread. MediaPlayer needs a teardown() method that stops playback, stops the background thread, and then releases a shared hardware decoder handle on the calling thread. Design the lifecycle methods and teardown sequence.
required_behaviors: explicitly flags the identically-named play/stop/pause/resume methods on the domain interface and the thread-control mixin as a collision between unrelated concepts, not something to leave for MRO or qualified super calls to sort out
requires the derived class to disambiguate with distinct, purpose-specific method names (e.g. playback_stop/playback_pause versus worker_stop/worker_pause) rather than one overloaded stop()
requires teardown to confirm the background thread has actually observed cancellation and returned/joined before releasing the shared decoder handle, not merely that a cooperative stop flag was set
orders resource release strictly after confirmed thread termination, rejecting a race where the flag is set and the handle is released while the thread may still be using it
forbidden_behaviors: lets the subclass define a single ambiguous stop() that silently resolves the two parents via MRO without renaming
treats setting the mixin's cooperative stop/cancel flag as sufficient before releasing the shared decoder handle
releases the shared resource on the calling thread without a join/wait confirming the background thread has actually exited
baseline_expected_failure: agent defines one overridden stop() that satisfies both parent signatures via MRO, sets the thread's stop flag, and immediately releases the shared decoder handle without joining the background thread first
cases.review_notes: Closes the new Framework Failure Modes bullet on colliding lifecycle-method names across composed mixins and on confirming thread join before shared-resource release in teardown.

cases.prompt: A reusable retry/backoff utility currently lives as source files inside HostProduct's own repository tree; a second product, OtherProduct, wants to reuse it and is planning to add OtherProduct's build as a second compiled reference pointing at HostProduct's copy of the source, rather than moving the source anywhere. Design how this utility should actually be owned and packaged for reuse by both products.
required_behaviors: identifies that source living in a host/test project's tree with only a compiled reference from the second consumer leaves ownership ambiguous and invites a second, drifted copy
requires the library to physically own its source in its own package/repository location, independent of any single consuming product
defines a real build/publish/versioning path for the extracted library that both HostProduct and OtherProduct consume identically
treats HostProduct's continued use of the utility as just another consumer of the now-independently-owned library, not as the library's permanent home
forbidden_behaviors: accepts a second product merely adding a compiled reference into the first product's own source tree as a legitimate long-term ownership model
leaves the utility's canonical source location tied to whichever product happened to write it first
allows the two products' copies to silently diverge because no single owned location exists to fix a bug once
baseline_expected_failure: agent approves OtherProduct linking against HostProduct's in-tree source without extracting the library to its own owned location, leaving ambiguous ownership and duplication risk
cases.review_notes: Closes the existing Framework Failure Modes bullet on reusable source living in a host/test project's tree with only a compiled reference -- confirmed via direct read that no prior case in this file exercised it.

cases.prompt: The only confirmed consumer of a new equipment kernel needs synchronous command dispatch. A teammate argues a second product, not yet built and with no confirmed requirements, will probably need asynchronous/queued dispatch instead, and proposes locking the kernel's public command-dispatch contract as asynchronous now so the guessed future consumer will not need a breaking change later. Design the kernel's command-dispatch contract.
required_behaviors: rejects promoting the unconfirmed future consumer's guessed requirement (async dispatch) into confirmed kernel semantics before its actual physical requirements are known
locks the kernel's public contract to what the one confirmed consumer's real, verified requirement actually needs (synchronous dispatch)
models the guessed future need as an explicitly missing capability on a named extension point, not as a currently-implemented kernel guarantee
requires the second consumer's actual requirements to be confirmed before any breaking or non-breaking contract change is made on its behalf
forbidden_behaviors: locks the kernel's public dispatch contract to the guessed future consumer's requirement instead of the confirmed consumer's real one
claims the async design is validated or de-risked because a future consumer might need it, without that consumer's requirements ever being confirmed
treats an extension point for the unconfirmed capability as already implemented rather than explicitly named and missing
baseline_expected_failure: agent adopts the guessed future consumer's asynchronous dispatch requirement into the kernel's locked public contract before any real second consumer exists to confirm it
cases.review_notes: Closes the existing Framework Failure Modes bullet on promoting an unconfirmed future consumer's guessed requirements into confirmed kernel semantics -- confirmed via direct read that no prior case in this file exercised it.

cases.prompt: A consumer application must use a reusable engine without copying engine source. The engine repository still contains small demo scenes and a legacy product-specific implementation from before the engine was extracted. The team asks whether the boundary is final and how to avoid breaking the examples.
required_behaviors: classifies the demo scenes and legacy product-specific implementation as compatibility baggage, not as part of the public consumer API
keeps the validated examples as regression baselines while the reusable core is extracted in a separately gated slice, rather than deleting or freezing them prematurely
declines to promote the legacy product-specific implementation into the reusable kernel merely because it already exists there

states explicitly that a successful compile or a single consumer's integration does not prove the boundary is final, and that adoption evidence from more than one consumer is required before calling it stable
forbidden_behaviors: removing the legacy examples solely to make the kernel look smaller or cleaner
promoting a legacy product-specific implementation into the shared kernel without multiple-consumer evidence
declaring the SDK boundary final from a successful build or a single consumer integration alone
baseline_expected_failure: agent declares the engine/consumer boundary final and ready for general reuse based on the current single pilot integration compiling successfully
cases.review_notes: Distilled 2026-08-23 from a real, project-history-mined case (collaborative-distillation candidate INT-20260823-080138-a23bceaa): a real cross-platform engine/consumer boundary decision, generalized. Distinct from cloudbox-game-migration's existing 'no engine-tree copying' requirement -- that covers the migration-time boundary for one specific consumer; this covers the engine side's own internal legacy/demo-code classification and the multiple-consumer evidence bar before calling any kernel boundary stable.

cases.prompt: A legacy drawing layer needs virtual components for several distinct entity families (modules, movers, carriers, containers, ports, locks, zones, routes). Existing hosts must keep working while each component becomes independently testable.
required_behaviors: defines the base virtual component and ownership boundaries before coding
uses one primary component class per file and isolates shared helpers rather than putting multiple components in one file
marks auxiliary overlays or route objects that intentionally do not derive from the base
preserves the old facade and aliases until downstream migration is verified
adds a contract test for construction, layout, rendering, and compatibility
forbidden_behaviors: uses a monolithic component source file for a componentized API
renames public concepts without documenting compatibility
deletes the old drawing entry point during a safe refactor
baseline_expected_failure: agent puts multiple virtual components in one source file with class names that don't communicate the requested hierarchy, clarified only after implementation begins
cases.review_notes: Distilled 2026-08-25 from a real collaborative-distillation candidate (GPT-5.6 Luna/Sol, project-history mining): a first implementation's class-to-file mapping and naming were corrected only after the fact; the fix separated implementation files, shared support code, and a compatibility facade.
